  "morbidity_events_gdft": {"value": "14 (28%)", "where": "Results (Table 5: Postoperative complications, n (%): group G 6 (12); includes POGI 12 (24%) and POGD 2 (4%), pneumonia 0, etc. Note: morbidity defined as any deviation from normal postoperative course per EPCO; total complications other than POGD = 6 (12%) + POGD (4%) + POGI (24%)? Clarify: \"The total number of patients with postoperative complication (except POGD) and the incidence of mortality\" recorded; Table 5 shows complications: pneumonia 0 vs 6 (12), wound infection 2 vs 5 (10), lower limb thrombosis 1 vs 6 (12), etc. Morbidity events (any complication except mortality) for group G = POGI 12 (24%) + complications other than POGD (e.g., pneumonia 0, wound infection 2, thrombosis 1) = total patients with any complication except POGD? Text: \"The total number of patients with postoperative complication (except POGD)\" recorded; but for extraction we need number of patients with at least one postoperative complication (morbidity). Table 5: \"Postoperative complications, n (%)\" includes pneumonia, wound infection, lower limb thrombosis; group G: pneumonia 0, wound infection 2 (4%), thrombosis 1 (2%) -> total complications other than POGD = 3 (6%); plus POGI (12 patients with score 3-5) and POGD (2 patients). Morbidity typically includes all postoperative complications; but field defined as \"number of patients with at least one postoperative complication\". From Table 5, group G: complications listed: wound infection 2 (4%), lower limb thrombosis 1 (2%), others 0; plus POGI (12 patients score 3-5) and POGD (2 patients score ≥6). POGI and POGD are GI intolerance/dysfunction per I-FEED; these are postoperative GI complications. So morbidity events (any complication) for group G = POGI (12) + POGD (2) + other (wound infection 2 + thrombosis 1) = 12+2+3=17? But POGI and POGD overlap? POGI defined as I-FEED 3-5 (intolerance), POGD ≥6 (dysfunction); I-FEED score recorded daily; POGD incidence 2/50 (4%), POGI incidence 12/50 (24%); other complications (pneumonia 0, wound infection 2, thrombosis 1) = 3; total patients with any postoperative complication = POGI (12) + other (3) = 15? However, POGI and POGD may overlap; but field says \"at least one postoperative complication\" generally. From text: \"The total number of patients with postoperative complication (except POGD) and the incidence of mortality during study period were recorded from the patient record... Complications were defined as any deviation from the normal postoperative course, guided by the European Perioperative Clinical Outcome (EPCO) definitions [22].\" Thus morbidity = patients with any complication per EPCO. Table 5 shows \"Postoperative complications, n (%)\" = 6 (12) for group G (includes wound infection 2, thrombosis 1, others 0? Actually table: Complications, n (%): Arrhythmia 1 (2), Pneumonia 0 (0), Lower limb thrombosis 1 (2), Wound infection 2 (4), Anastomotic fistula 0, Hemorrhage 1 (2). So total complications (excluding pneumonia since pneumonia 0) = 1+2+1+2 =6? Arrhythmia 1, thrombosis 1, wound infection 2, hemorrhage 1 = total 5? But table shows 6 (12) for group G? Wait Table 5: \"Postoperative complications, n (%)\" row: group G 6 (12); details: Arrhythmia 1 (2), Pneumonia 0 (0), Lower limb thrombosis 1 (2), Wound infection 2 (4), Anastomotic fistula 0, Hemorrhage 1 (2). Sum =1+0+1+2+0+1=5? But written as 6 (12%) suggests including all listed complications as separate events? Possibly count patients with any complication; group G had 6 patients with complications (1 arrhythmia, 1 thrombosis, 2 wound infection, 1 hemorrhage =5 patients? Might be 6 due to overlap? However, safest is to use the reported \"Postoperative complications, n (%)\" value from Table 5: group G 6 (12%), group C 13 (26%). Thus morbidity_events_gdft = 6 (12 patients), morbidity_events_control = 13 (26 patients). We'll extract the number of patients (6 for G, 13 for C) as reported in Table 5.", "where": "Results (Table 5: Postoperative complications, n (%): group G 6 (12), group C 13 (26))"},
